Specification: This module specifies the consensus problem, which requires a set of processes to agree on a single value. The specification focuses on the core aspect of consensus: the selection of a single value from a set of possible values (Value), abstracting away the details of proposing and learning values. The safety property is modeled by allowing only a single state change in which the variable 'chosen' transitions from the empty set to a singleton set containing a value from Value, or remains unchanged. The module defines both safety (at most one value is chosen) and liveness (eventually some value is chosen, under fairness and non-emptiness assumptions) properties, and includes TLAPS proofs of invariance and liveness. Notably, the specification is minimal, with only one variable and a trivial next-state relation, and uses both temporal and fairness properties.
